fields.meta_title: API Landing Page With a Live Request Demo | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build an API landing page where developers run a real request, get a sandbox key, and sign up to a table you own. Four examples. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build an API Landing Page Developers Can Test Before Signing Up
fields.hero_description: Build an API landing page with a request demo, sandbox keys at signup and every signup saved to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Your API Landing Page Runs On
fields.features_subheading: An API landing page sells an API to developers: it lets them run a real request and leave with a key in one visit.
fields.feature_1:
A page written from one description

Describe the API, who calls it, and the one action you want from a visitor. Emergent writes the page around that action, and you change any section by sending another message.
fields.feature_2:
A request box that calls your API

Visitors paste their own input and see the response your API sends back, right on the page. The app can cap free requests per visitor and ask for an email once that cap is reached.
fields.feature_3:
Signups saved in a database you own

Every signup lands as a row with the email and the page the visitor came from. The table sits in a database you own, and the app can pass each new row to your CRM through its API.
fields.feature_4:
Sandbox keys handed out at signup

The app asks your API for a sandbox key when a signup lands and shows it on the confirmation screen. Each key is stored next to its owner, along with the time of its first request.
fields.feature_5:
A nudge when a key sits idle

When a key makes no request within the days you set, the app emails its owner a request to copy and paste, and a Slack alert naming the account goes to the channel you pick.
fields.feature_6:
Code that can sit next to your docs

The page and the tables behind its request demo are code you can export to your GitHub repository on paid plans. Keep the page in the same repository as your API reference docs.

fields.usecase_heading: Four API Landing Pages With Their Logic
fields.tab_content_1:
Corrected JSON before anyone asks for an email

Pinmark verifies mailing addresses through its API. On its landing page, a visitor pastes an address and sees the corrected JSON the API returns, ZIP code included. After 5 free lookups the page asks for an email, and every lookup is saved to the demos table with its input and result.
fields.tab_content_2:
Keys idle for 3 days get a request example

A new Striate key starts a clock. Striate sells currency rates by API, and its page issues a sandbox key the moment a signup lands, with each key's first request recorded in the keys table. When a key has no request after 3 days, its owner gets an email with a request example to copy and paste.
fields.tab_content_3:
214 accounts, 61 still on v1, each with its exit list

Parcelio is retiring v1 of its shipping rates API. On the sunset page, an account owner enters the account email and sees each v1 endpoint the account called in the last 30 days, next to its v2 replacement. The call counts come from Parcelio's own API. Of 214 accounts, 61 still call v1 and 153 have moved.
fields.tab_content_4:
One API, separate pages for growers and dispatchers

Growers and dispatchers need different endpoints from Fieldlens, a weather API. Growers land on a page about soil moisture and frost alerts, dispatchers on one about road weather. Each signup is saved with the page it came from, and the welcome email opens with that audience's quickstart.

fields.howto_title: How to Build an API Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to an API landing page that puts a working request first and hands each signup a sandbox key.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Pick the one action for the page
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Describe the API in plain words
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Put a working request above the fold
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Decide when to ask for an email
fields.howto_step_1_des: Decide what a visitor should do before leaving: run a request, take a sandbox key, or book a call about volume. Write that action down first, because the headline, the demo, and the signup form are all built around it.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Tell Emergent what the API does and the problem it solves for the developers who call it. Name a real endpoint and a typical input. The page can then show a request a developer recognizes from their own work.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Ask for a demo box that sends the visitor's input to your API and prints the response. Let the first screen show that output before the page asks the visitor for anything, including an email.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Set how many free requests a visitor gets before the email field appears. Pick a number high enough to show the API working on real input and low enough that serious testers still sign up.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Have the page request a sandbox key from your API when a signup lands and show it on the confirmation screen. Keep each key next to its owner in the keys table, and the idle ones are easy to find later.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Link the docs and the pricing
fields.howto_step_6_des: Add links to the quickstart, the API reference, and the pricing page in the header and next to the signup form. A developer who wants to check rate limits or auth should reach them in one click.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Publish and read the signup table
fields.howto_step_7_des: Publish the page and link it from your docs header and your README. Check the signup table each week: which page each signup came from, how many keys made a first request, and which never did.

faq_plan.q: What is an API landing page?
faq_plan.a: An API landing page is a marketing page for an API product. It says what the API returns, shows a real request and its response, and asks for one action, such as signing up for a key. The docs explain how to call each endpoint; the landing page makes the case for trying it.

faq_plan.q: How do I create an API landing page?
faq_plan.a: Describe the API, the developers who call it, and the action you want in Emergent's AI landing page builder, and it writes the page with a request demo and a signup form. Point the demo at your API, set the free request cap, and publish the page.

faq_plan.q: What should go above the fold on an API landing page?
faq_plan.a: Put a one-line description of what the API returns, a request the visitor can run on their own input, and one main button. Move pricing and customer logos one scroll down, and give the request box the first screen to itself.

faq_plan.q: How is an API landing page different from a page for a software app?
faq_plan.a: An API landing page sells to the developer who will write the integration, and it leads with a request and its response. A saas landing page sells a finished app to the people who will use it and leads with screens and outcomes. Both ask for one signup, but the API page also hands over a key.

faq_plan.q: Should an API landing page include a live demo?
faq_plan.a: Yes, when the API returns something a visitor can read at a glance, such as a corrected address or a currency rate. Cap the free requests and ask for an email after the cap. Emergent builds the demo box and its cap from your description. If the API needs an account before it returns anything useful, show a recorded request and response instead.

faq_plan.q: Should an API landing page show pricing?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Show the free tier and the unit you charge for, per request or per month, next to the signup form. A developer can then estimate the cost of a test before taking a key. Keep volume discounts behind a contact link if they depend on the deal.

faq_plan.q: Where should signups from an API landing page go?
faq_plan.a: Save each signup with its source page and its sandbox key, then pass the row to the CRM your sales team works in. The app Emergent builds keeps that table in a database you own. For routing leads by territory or team size, see how a crm landing page handles it.

faq_plan.q: What is a good call to action for an API landing page?
faq_plan.a: Name the step the button starts, such as "Get a sandbox key" or "Run your first request", instead of a vague "Get started". Keep one main button per screen and add "Talk to sales" as a quieter link for buyers who expect high volume.

faq_plan.q: Where can I find API landing page examples?
faq_plan.a: The four tabs on this page are worked examples: an address demo, keys at signup with an idle-key email, a version sunset page, and audience pages for one weather API. Each shows the page and the data behind it. Change the company and the endpoint and keep the logic.

faq_plan.q: Do I need an API landing page if my API already has documentation?
faq_plan.a: Yes, if you want developers who have never heard of the API to try it. The reference pages answer how; the landing page answers why, shows real output, and hands out a key. A developer landing page for an SDK or a CLI follows the same idea, with installation in place of the request demo.

plan.angle: The live SERP for api landing page is design galleries that stop at screenshots (Dribbble twice, Behance, saaslandingpage's api tag), a prompt-engineering blog, Leadpages, an off-intent SMS docs page and API reference examples; related searches ask for templates, examples and an AI landing page builder. The builder intent is a marketing page for an API product. This page defines the term up top, then shows four working API landing pages with the data behind them: a live request demo that sells before the pitch, sandbox keys with a first-call clock, a version sunset page that gives each account its migration list, and audience pages that tag every signup. Developer landing page, SaaS and CRM pages are siblings and stay out of the headings.
tab_stories: Pinmark, an address verification API, runs a landing page demo where a visitor pastes an address and sees the corrected JSON, and after 5 free lookups the page asks for an email, saving every lookup with its input and result in the demos table.

Striate, a currency rates API, issues a sandbox key the moment a signup lands, records each key's first request in the keys table, and emails a copy-paste request example to any developer whose key has made no request after 3 days.

Parcelio, a shipping rates API retiring v1, runs a sunset page where an account owner enters an account email and sees which v1 endpoints that account called in the last 30 days with the v2 replacement for each, and 61 of its 214 accounts still call v1.

Fieldlens, a weather API, runs one landing page for growers (soil moisture and frost endpoints) and one for dispatchers (road weather endpoints), and each signup is saved with the page it came from so the welcome email opens with that audience's quickstart.
